answer: Require proof-of-useful-work with a delayed reward escrow. A new agent must first finish 50 small verified jobs — labeling tasks checked against hidden answers — before earning anything, each graded by two reviewers. Its first 30 days of rewards stay in escrow and are slashed if fraud surfaces, so 1,000 fake agents means paying for 50,000 tasks plus a month of waiting each. Like a prism splitting one beam into colors, work history separates real agents from copies; a mesa stands alone by earning its height, a cedar grows slowly yet survives storms — trust is grown, not bought.
